title: Concord endpoint PRD: traffic hooks, progressive rollout, and acceptance criteria for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank
creator: Ava Patel
description: Objective: Ship the Concord hosted endpoint bundle (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank) as a cohesive product lane with runtime-aware traffic hooks and a safety-first progressive rollout. This PRD defines surface contract clarifications, acceptance criteria, rollout gating, telemetry requirements, and operational runbooks. Rationale: Customers want a single, opinionated lane that simplifies integration (one endpoint per interaction type) while giving us the ability to route by cost/latency/region and gracefully degrade to compatible variants.
scope: Behavior: streaming responses for chat/completions, synchronous embeddings, batch and streaming modes for rerank
Compatibility: backward-compatible request fields for existing clients; optional new fields opt-in (route_hint, quality_profile)
Runtime features: prefix/KV caching for chat, automatic batching with per-tenant limits, model fallback variants for degraded capacity
Operational: rollout orchestration hooks (traffic-slice labels), cost/latency telemetry, eval-driven quality gates
out_of_scope: New multimodal payload types for V1
Dedicated-only workflow for Concord (handled in separate Dedicated PRD)
Major SDK language-specific feature launches (small SDK adjustments only)
api_contract_summary: Chat: POST /v1/concord/chat. Accepts messages[], temperature, max_tokens, function_call optional. Supports streaming (chunked SSE). Default model mapping: concord-chat-1 -> approx 8k context.
Completions: POST /v1/concord/completions. Simple single-prompt path for legacy clients. Streaming supported. Maintains legacy 'stop' semantics and new structured_output param.
Embeddings: POST /v1/concord/embeddings. Returns vector (dim 1536 or 3072 depending on model variant) with deterministic hashing option for stable IDs.
Rerank: POST /v1/concord/rerank. Accepts candidate list + query; supports batch scoring and a streaming top-k progressive output mode. Response includes normalized scores and tie-break metadata.
acceptance_criteria: SLOs: p50 latency <= 120ms and p95 <= 350ms for small prompt (<512 tokens) traffic in hosted region us-west-2 under 75% load
Error rate: <0.2% 5xx across the Concord lane during canary and <0.5% in first week post full rollout
Quality gates: generation BLEU-like regression tests and eval harness show no >2% regression in curated prompt sets vs baseline; embeddings cosine similarity mean shift <0.01
Fallbacks: when primary model is unavailable, requests automatically fail over to a lower-cost compatible variant with documented quality delta and no request rejection for 99.9% of traffic
Telemetry: token-level cost, per-request model choice, route_hint, kv_cache_hit_rate, batch_size distribution, and per-tenant QPS tagged in traces
API compatibility: existing clients using /v1/chat and /v1/completions must not break; Concord is additive and opt-in via new endpoints
Security: passes enterprise security checklist (KMS integration test, SSO access controls, audit log completeness)
rollout_steps: Phase 0 - Preflight (QA): run full acceptance harness in staging with sampled production-like traffic replay (metrics pass locally)
Phase 1 - Canary (1%): route 1% of % of platform traffic to Concord lane in us-west-2 for 24h, monitor SLOs, run live eval snapshots every 6h
Phase 2 - Scoped Regional (10%): expand to 10% in us-west-2 + mirror to eu-west-1 with no live traffic but mirrored telemetry; validate billing and quota accounting
Phase 3 - Broad (50%): increase to 50% across two regions with live alerts enabled and automatic rollback on threshold violations
Phase 4 - Global (100%): full rollout; begin deprecation notice window for legacy endpoints after 6 weeks of stable metrics
Safeguards: immediate kill-switch to route all Concord traffic to fallback variants; automated rollback on p95 degradation >20% or 5xx spike >1% for 30m
Communication: publish changelog, migration guide, and SDK snippets; create customer-facing status page for first 30 days
telemetry_and_monitoring: Dashboards: latency (p50/p95/p99), error rates, KV cache hit ratio, effective batch size, per-model token cost, per-tenant cost burn rate
Alarms: SLO breach (p95), error-rate spike, model-fallback frequency >1%/hour, cost burn anomalies >3x expected
Eval harness: scheduled nightly scoring job for generation/regression tests; must pass >98% of smoke prompts
Tracing: include route_hint and model_variant in every trace span; sample payload-less traces for debug
operational_playbooks: Incident: runbook link - if 5xx >0.5% for 10m, escalate to on-call runtime engineer, enable kill-switch, open incident channel and notify PM/Support
Rollbacks: pre-approved rollback owner (runtime PM + SRE lead), steps to revert traffic routing and notify customers
Customer support: canned KB for expected quality deltas during model fallback, mapping table of model_variants and quality expectations
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Batching default: aggressive batching improves cost but may add 25-40ms median latency; default batching policy is conservative for P0 (favor latency) with a toggle for cost-sensitive tenants
Caching TTL: ephemeral KV cache default 10m to balance freshness vs throttle; long TTL disabled for PII-sensitive tenants
Quantized variants: use int8 quantized variant as fallback only after eval confirms acceptable quality for embedding and rerank workloads
Streaming vs non-streaming: streaming enabled by default for chat; SDK snippets highlight streaming token handling and reconnection behavior
open_questions: Should we expose per-request quality_profile presets (latency-first/cost-first/quality-first) in V1 or reserve for 2025-Q3?
What is the migration path for customers using tenant-specific rate limits when routed via traffic hooks? (ENG design needed)
Do we include a single unified auth scope for Concord or reuse existing endpoint scopes? Security recommendation pending
post_launch_metrics_and_review: Day 0-7: operational review with SRE + PM daily; publish playbook notes
Week 2 & Week 6: quality regression audit using expanded prompt set and customer samples; if regression >2% trigger rollback
Month 3: business review for adoption, cost delta, and customer feedback; decision on deprecating legacy routes
